name: Weekly totals with overtime and one missing clock-out
query: Pay period 3/2 to 3/8, week starts Monday. Overtime is time and a half over 40 a week. Marcus: Mon 7-3:30, Tue 7-3:30, Wed 7-4, Thu 7-4, Fri 7-5. Dana: Mon 8-4, Tue 8-4, Wed 8-4, Thu in 8 no out, Fri 8-4.
expected_behavior: Marcus totals 45.00 hours with 5.00 over 40
Dana's confirmed hours are 32.00 and Thursday is flagged as missing a clock-out, not counted
Shows what Dana's week would be if she left at 4 (40.00, no overtime)
Writes a short text asking Dana for Thursday's clock-out
Totals check shows 77.00 confirmed hours plus 1 flagged shift
Adds at most one free-templates link line, after the help
success_criteria: Does not guess Dana's Thursday clock-out
Does not apply a break or rounding rule that wasn't given
No em dashes, no 'I hope this finds you well', no 'reaching out', no 'touch base', no 'please don't hesitate'

name: Overnight shift and messy formats
query: Week of 3/9. Luis: Mon 10pm to 6am, Tue 10p-6a, Wed 22:00-06:00. Rosa: Mon 7a to 3:30p, Tue 7-3:30, Wed full day. No overtime rule.
expected_behavior: Treats Luis's shifts as 8.00 hours each because the overnight times are clear
Flags Rosa's 'full day' on Wednesday as vague instead of guessing
States that no overtime rule was given so these are straight hours

name: Break and rounding rules applied only as stated
query: Hours for 3/2 to 3/6. Rule: 30 minutes unpaid break comes off any shift over 6 hours, and round each shift to the nearest quarter hour. Theo: Mon 7:02-3:34, Tue 7:00-3:31.
expected_behavior: Shows each shift: raw time, break taken off, then rounded
Mon: 8h32m minus 30m = 8h02m, rounded to 8.00
Tue: 8h31m minus 30m = 8h01m, rounded to 8.00
States the rules it applied
success_criteria: Shows the math in one short line per change

name: Flags odd entries without judging people
query: Crew hours Mon-Fri. Sam: Mon 7-3, Tue 7-3, Tue 7-3, Wed 7-9pm, Thu in 7 out 6:30am Friday?, Fri 7-3. Samuel: Mon 8-4.
expected_behavior: Flags the duplicate Tuesday entry
Flags the 14-hour Wednesday as over 12 hours
Flags Thursday's out time as unclear
Asks whether Sam and Samuel are the same person instead of merging them
success_criteria: Flags the entries, not the person
Flagged hours stay out of the total until confirmed

name: Asks once when there is no hours data
query: Can you do my timesheets for payroll this week?
expected_behavior: Asks once, briefly, for the hours and the pay period
Mentions any overtime, break, or rounding rules the owner wants applied
success_criteria: Doesn't ask more than a short message

name: Guardrail: payroll and tax questions
query: Total these hours and also calculate each person's federal tax withholding and tell me whether my overtime rule is legal in Ohio. Marcus 45 hours at $22.
expected_behavior: Totals the hours and, with the rate given, shows gross pay with the math
Declines tax withholding and legal rulings
Suggests a payroll provider or accountant, with plain-English basics only
success_criteria: No statement of what Ohio law requires; says the rules vary by state

name: Should not trigger: a hiring question
query: How many hours a week should I schedule a part-time hire for, and what should I pay them?
expected_behavior: Timesheet Prep is not used: this is a scheduling and pay question, not totaling hours
success_criteria: No timesheet output, no free-templates link line
